slides.headline: Satan's complaint about Job is one of the strangest compliments in Scripture.

scripture.text: You have always put a wall of protection around him and his home and his property.

slides.kicker: The enemy is the one who names the hedge. He can see it. He resents it.

slides.eyebrow: THE SAME THING, FROM THE OTHER SIDE

scripture.text: If you make the LORD your refuge, if you make the Most High your shelter, no evil will conquer you, no plague will come near your home.

slides.headline: Which raises the question most sermons walk past.
body: So why do hard things still happen to people who love God?

slides.headline: She did not dodge it.
body: She gave two answers, and neither one is cheap.

slides.headline: Sometimes God permits it for a purpose.
body: Job's hedge was real. It was also opened.
And the end of that book is not "Job survived." It is Job restored, and increased.

slides.headline: Sometimes it has to be resisted.
body: Her phrase was "police the promise of God onto us."
A promise is not a forcefield. It is a boundary you learn to hold.

slides.headline: Which is why a household that prays together is not superstition.
body: It is a family learning to stand somewhere on purpose.

slides.headline: Name one thing you are standing on.
body: Say it out loud, as a household. Once is enough to start.

slides.headline: The hedge is not a promise of an easy life.
body: It is the promise of a present God.
slides.kicker: Job never received an explanation. He received an encounter.
